newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - October 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - October 25.

text.p: Following are the highlights of stories reported in the Irish press on Friday.

- There was increasing concern in the Irish beef industry on Thursday over the growing number of BSE cases after Ireland's Agriculture Minister Ivan Yates announced that three more cases have been discovered in the Republic of Ireland.

- A group from Dundalk on Thursday won the right to take legal action against the British Sellafield nuclear plant, but the Irish government insisted it was awaiting the Attorney General's approval before it could do the same.
- The Irish pound crept back above 1.01 against sterling on Thursday as a number of experts warned of increased currency and interest rate volatility in the run-up to a single European currency.

- Almost three quarters of companies in the Irish Financial Services Center have to recruit experienced people from abroad because they cannot find them here, a survey published on Thursday by Irish executive search firm Amrop International Ireland said.
- Police are concerned the IRA might be planning attacks on suspected drug dealers in Dublin under cover of the anti-drugs campaigns in the city.
- Enterprise and employment minster Richard Bruton has launched a scathing attack on the board of Irish Press Publications for the delay in putting its newspaper titles on the market.
